notes: Accuracy release — every number Helix shows was audited against Windows itself, and nine bugs that made it report the wrong thing are fixed. Disk Health was silently dead (an import error hid the card entirely) and now reports your drive model, SMART status, media and bus type. Startup Apps was wrong four ways: it counted a phantom registry entry, treated entries you had switched off in Task Manager as if they still ran, and never looked at the 32-bit registry key or either Startup folder — it now reads all five sources, shows disabled entries badged as off, and classifies by what an entry actually launches instead of its registry name (so OneDrive and Realtek audio are no longer counted as your personal apps). That alone removed a fabricated 20-point health deduction. The health score and the Findings list are now computed from the same list, so they can no longer disagree, and the startup threshold matches between the score and the chip. Event log asked for 24 hours but delivered about 90 minutes and hid 16 of 19 errors behind DNS and wifi warnings — errors and warnings are now queried separately and errors are never truncated. Top Processes listed the kernel's Memory Compression as the biggest consumer and measured browsers one process at a time; memory is now summed per app with the instance count shown, and the 'one app is hogging memory' warning is judged as a share of installed RAM rather than a flat ceiling. Duplicate Files returned different results on identical runs; the scan is now deterministic, groups by size before hashing, and reads files in chunks instead of loading them whole. Small windows also scroll properly now, so the bottom of a page is always reachable. Keeps every 1.1.4/1.1.5 security invariant (trusted host, SHA256-verified download, 128 MiB cap, no visible terminals, below-normal CPU and I/O priority).
